transcript: Seeing Oh, Mary! at the Lucille Lortel Theater was one of the most enjoyable theater going experiences I've had in awhile. In this new comedy written by and starring Cole Escola as Mary Todd Lincoln, we see a series of brief scenes leading up to Abraham Lincoln's assassination. This is historical fiction at its most loose and its most hilarious. For example, a major plotline involves Mary taking up acting lessons that Lincoln signs her up for just as a way to keep her from bothering him. This show is queer, it is camp, and the characters say truly out of pocket things. The unapologetic ridiculousness of the whole thing is what really sells it, as is the physical comedy by all of the actors. I think comedy is very hard to do well so I was really impressed by this piece. Oh, Mary! is currently running until early May. With that, another program for my collection.
